summary: Finite rahəṭ/rahiṭo/rahiṭi, motion Part act. rahoṭo/rahaṭto/rahoṭe, and Infinitiv rahṭo remain distinct. Bare rahoṭo can accompany both feminine and plural controllers (56/58; 69/491); do not normalize agreement.

Infectum describes ongoing or narrative running, and Infectum-wa habitual capacity or repeated responses. Direction and extent complements are not patient objects; b-marked horses at 78/45 specify mounted running.

29/183 is already quoted in BOTH Preterit Intransitive and Infinitiv; the reader claim that the finite verb is only collateral in an Infinitiv example is false. Existing JL 12.13.8, LuF snake Infinitiv, LuF running child, 1/55, 73/69, 115/80 and LB 203 are not duplicated.
A lookup for raġloṯe b found no collocation. JTM 5.2/21 supplies the vivid running phrase retained below. Lookup marhaṭ found established horse causatives but no pre-existing flight idiom.

summary: Snakes, goats, insects, a rope mistaken for a snake, and water extend the runner participant; the water riddle deliberately applies running to something without feet.
rahoṭo can characterize a runner by habitual capacity (73/348, 351), beside simultaneous running with motion verbs. This is nominal use of Part act., not a distinct running sense.
Money and work become figurative pursuit goals with bəṯr in the nominal phrase ṭerhiṭo bəṯr. Morphological relation to Infinitiv rahṭo remains open; no new numbered verbal sense.
Human child as causee with feminine agent marhəṭlali extends the inherited horse causative; the context of forcing a child inside does not require the round-1 military defeat sense III.2.
